subject: TLS lifecycle & load-balancer termination — key rotation and HSM evidence request
messages:
From: Paul Lin <paul.lin@emeraldbank.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request — TLS key rotation logs + LB termination details

Hi Aditya,

Our security team is wrapping up the SIG/SOC2 pre-audit and we have a few specific follow-ups related to TLS and key management for the Redwood-hosted endpoints used by Emerald Bank. Can you provide evidence for the following items?

1) End-to-end TLS lifecycle for client connections that terminate at Redwood-managed load balancers (diagram + description of where TLS keys live).
2) Logs showing regular TLS certificate/key rotation for the last 12 months (or rotation policy + representative log slice).
3) Confirmation that private keys for certs used in termination are HSM-backed or KMS-wrapped, and the attestation we can share with auditors.
4) For TLS session keys and ephemeral keying material, any info on whether keys are ephemeral only and not persistently stored.

We'd like this by EOD Friday so we can feed into the audit pack. If any item requires legal/infosec review to share, flag it and we'll coordinate.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Lin
Security Engineer — Emerald Bank
security@emeraldbank.com
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Paul Lin <paul.lin@emeraldbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — TLS key rotation logs + LB termination details

Paul — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (security/compliance) and Jasmine (infra/runbooks). We can provide what you asked; below is our proposed evidence package and timeline.

Summary of what we will deliver (target delivery: Friday EOD, Nov 13):
- Architecture diagram (lb-termination-architecture-2026-11.pdf) showing where TLS termination happens and where private keys are stored.
- Rotation logs for certs that terminate on Redwood-managed LB: redwood-tls-rotation-log-2026Q3.csv (sampled entries spanning last 12 months) + our rotation policy excerpt.
- HSM attestation PDF for keys used in cert provisioning and wrapping: hsm-attestation-statement-2026-10.pdf. This shows that cert private keys are generated/wrapped with a customer-segregated KMS/HSM workflow when required.
- Short technical note on ephemeral session keys: AES/GCM session keys are negotiated per-TLS session and not persisted beyond session lifetime; we will include a concise explanation.

Constraints / notes:
- We cannot share raw private key material. Attestation and signed statements plus rotation logs are typical and should satisfy auditors.
- Some attestation docs include sensitive operator metadata; we'll redact operator identifiers but include unique request IDs so Emerald's auditors can trace.

If that plan works I'll package the PDFs and CSV slice and share a Drive link. If you need custody-level proofs (live HSM console snapshots), that's a legal/contract item — we may need a short NDA addendum.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Paul Lin <paul.lin@emeraldbank.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — TLS key rotation logs + LB termination details

Paul — attached the initial package here and a very short runbook excerpt. See attachments: lb-termination-architecture-2026-11.pdf, redwood-tls-rotation-log-2026Q3.csv, hsm-attestation-statement-2026-10.pdf.

Attachment notes (quick hits):
- lb-termination-architecture-2026-11.pdf: shows two termination modes (edge TLS at Redwood-managed LB, and passthrough for BYO-certs). Diagram highlights that keys for Redwood-managed certs are stored in an HSM-accessible KMS partition with strict ACLs; we state retention and key derivation boundaries.
- redwood-tls-rotation-log-2026Q3.csv: curated slice covering rotations and issuance events for your tenant space; includes timestamps, cert thumbprint, rotation trigger (policy/expiry/incident), and rotation request id. We removed internal requestor UPNs and replaced them with opaque request ids.
- hsm-attestation-statement-2026-10.pdf: vendor-signed statement detailing HSM model, FIPS/SIG levels, and a hash of the key-wrapping policy. We can provide additional console audit extracts under NDA.

Short answers to your numbered items:
1) Architecture diagram + description: included.
2) Rotation logs: CSV slice included; full log export is available under a compliance request.
3) HSM/KMS confirmation: see attestation PDF; keys used for cert private material are either generated inside HSM or imported wrapped by KMS with HSM-backed key wrapping.
4) Ephemeral session keys: not stored; see runbook excerpt page 2.

Next steps: if Emerald auditors need an expanded log set or an auditor-facing attestation letter on Redwood letterhead, reply with the auditor contact and we will route to Legal for a signed attestation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Security Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Paul Lin <paul.lin@emeraldbank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — TLS key rotation logs + LB termination details

Marissa / Aditya — got the package, thanks. Quick confirmation items from our side after reviewing:

• The CSV slice looks sufficient for now; auditors asked whether the rotation requests have an immutable identifier tied to an enrollment event — the request ids you supplied are perfect.
• For the HSM attestation PDF: can Redwood provide an auditor-facing cover letter on Redwood letterhead that references the attestation PDF and authorizes auditors to verify the HSM vendor signature? They want a direct contact for any vendor-level verification.
• For BYO-cert passthrough mode: please confirm that in passthrough mode we do not hand keys to Redwood and that connection metrics still show TLS session negotiation at the LB (for performance tracing). A one-line confirmation will do.

If you can send the cover letter and the one-line BYO-cert confirmation, we can close this item and attach to the SIG pack. Thanks again — tight timeline appreciated.

—Paul

On Fri, 13 Nov 2026 at 15:45 Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Paul — noted. Marissa and I will arrange an auditor cover letter from Legal (we'll route the request and aim to deliver next week).
>
> BYO-cert passthrough confirmation (short): In passthrough mode Redwood does not persist or escrow customer private keys; certificates are presented by customer-owned endpoints and TLS handshake termination for passthrough is performed upstream of Redwood-managed LB. Connection/session metrics remain available for performance tracing but do not include customer private key material.
>
> I'll follow up when the letter is ready.
>
> —Aditya
